title: Seminuclear Flip Phacoemulsification for Soft Nuclear Cataract Surgery: A New Soft Nucleus Cataract Chopping Technique
indication: Age-related soft nuclear cataract (Emery-Little grade 1-2), age over 50 years, preoperative ECD above 1200 cells/mm2; previous intraocular surgery, corneal disease, glaucoma, uveitis, axial length outside 22-28 mm and zonular weakness excluded

groups.description: Seminuclear flip phacoemulsification (SNFP), the new soft-nucleus chopping technique declared as the experimental arm; randomized block design stratified by nuclear grade; Infiniti torsional mode, 2.8 mm temporal clear corneal incision; single surgeon

Conventional quick-chop phacoemulsification (QCP), the study's control group; randomized block design stratified by nuclear grade; Infiniti torsional mode, 2.8 mm temporal clear corneal incision; single surgeon

series.baseline_label: Preoperative central corneal ECD of the operated eye (Table 4 row 'Preoperative central corneal endothelial cell density'; Topcon SP-2000)
series.notes: Table 4 column 'SNFP group (n = 87)'; mean ± SD (Results: 'mean central corneal endothelial cell density'). Only preoperative and 1-month ECD were measured. Per-visit n not tabulated.

series.baseline_label: Preoperative central corneal ECD of the operated eye (Table 4 row 'Preoperative central corneal endothelial cell density'; Topcon SP-2000)
series.notes: Table 4 column 'QCP group (n = 89)'; mean ± SD (Results: 'mean central corneal endothelial cell density'). Only preoperative and 1-month ECD were measured. Results: postoperative outcome data of the 2 QCP eyes with posterior capsule rupture were excluded, so the 1-month mean likely covers 87 eyes; the table header gives n = 89.

exclusions.reason: Test statistics and p-values are not admissible
Model-adjusted values in text, not tabulated group means

notes: The article introduces SNFP as a new technique and calls QCP the control group (randomized): SNFP is the treated (investigational technique) arm and QCP the control arm.
Two posterior capsule ruptures in the QCP group were managed with anterior vitrectomy and sulcus IOL; their postoperative data were excluded by the authors.
